FinTechs scale on decision speed: onboarding, fraud, credit and compliance must run real-time under regulatory scrutiny that grows with their size. The platforms that industrialize decisioning and evidence early avoid the mid-scale stall.

items: Ring fraud and account abuse scale faster than rules.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Lakehouse Architecture & Migration, Advanced Risk & Predictive Analytics, Real-Time Streaming & Event-Driven Decisioning from the Data, Analytics & Lakehouse tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Onboarding/KYC, Fraud decisioning, Credit underwriting) on Dataq Forge and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — AML/CTF among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Metrics into management: one governed semantic layer, decision cadence built in.
One customer, one product, one truth: MDM and catalog discipline that regulators can read.
Forward-looking risk on governed data: credit, insurance, operational and market models that explain themselves.
Consented alternative data into underwriting (approval quality up)

blocks.x: At industry level, the same pattern

At Technology & SaaS level this capability reads as: clean rooms, entitlements and metering for customer-facing insights (second revenue line launched). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

A fixed rhythm keeps progress visible from week one — here is the one we run. Weeks 1–2 belong to measurement: the baseline metric is captured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 run a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — steered by a control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 convert the pilot into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, and close with a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses a gate is stopped or redirected on the record.
